interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation â€” checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage

physical_description.visible_augmentations: Chrome circuitry visible at temple installations and jawline surgical sites â€” synthetic blood gives her skin a faintly luminescent quality under neon. No traditional prosthetics; all work is internal except the visible scarring.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with biomechanical precision â€” every motion calibrated and efficient. No fidgeting, no wasted energy. When standing still, weight rests on the balls of her feet. When walking, she moves low and centered, ready to shift direction. Eyes are always cataloging â€” exits, sightlines, potential threats. Rare to see her relaxed; even at rest, there is coiled readiness.

Form-fitting tactical pants with cargo pockets and reinforced knee areas â€” expects to move fast and possibly crawl. Black steel-toed boots, minimalist and broken in. Layered with a charcoal undershirt. No visible corporate branding or crew colors. Carries a small satchel with modular pockets for tools. Everything is dark, functional, and replaceable. Clothes are equipment, not identity.
